_comment: North America stage trackers. 'nations' fills every polygon by the power that holds it (src/us/powers.json). 'states' fills Newberry's U.S. polygons by their TERR_TYPE, as Newberry classifies them; everything else is muted. 'cessions' shades the Royce land cessions made up to the date shown, stepped by period (a sequential key: darker is later); everything else is muted.

states.title: States and territories
states._other_areas: Newberry's 'Other' polygons this tracker names for what they were, by Newberry id (statehood deck brief, 2026-11-18, item 4): each keeps the hatch (each overlapped or was disputed by another claim) and takes a key line of its own in place of 'Disputed or overlapping claims'. Oregon Country and the Uncertain Boundary Area are joint or disputed areas and keep their claim lines ('Claimed by the United States and Britain'). Under the nations tracker nothing changes: there the republics are keyed by their sides (owner, 2026-11-09).

ds_deseret.label: Proposed state (not recognized)
ds_deseret._why: Newberry's own record: 'The General Assembly of the newly proposed state of Deseret met on 2 Jul 1849 ... but proposal never gained support in U.S. Congress.' It overlapped the Mexican Cession, then Utah, New Mexico and Oregon Territories and California.

vt_republic.label: Independent republic
vt_republic._why: Newberry's own record: 'Vermont functioned as an independent republic until statehood in 1791', its independence from New York not recognized by the Continental Congress.

tx_republic.label: Independent republic
tx_republic._why: Newberry's own record: 'Texas declared its independence from Mexico'; Mexico did not recognize it before annexation (the land both claimed is OpenHistoricalMap's Joint Mexico-Texas Claim, hatched in its own right).

slavery.title: Free and slave states
slavery._comment: Each state filled by its status in a table, data/us/slavery-status.csv (src/us/slavery.js): one row per Newberry polygon id per status period, with a source. A territory without a row takes one neutral fill; the District of Columbia and joint or disputed areas stay paper. 'coverage' is the span the rows were entered for (1 January 1820 to 31 December 1860, in which no state changed status): outside it no state is given a status and the legend says so. Rows are TEST ROWS until the owner reviews them (brief of 2026-11-16).
slavery.uncovered: Status is entered for 1820 to 1860 only

freeblack.title: Free Black population
freeblack._comment: The slavery tracker's fills (free state, slave state, territories; its table and its coverage), with a number badge on each of the ten states where the census on or before the date counted the most free Black people, and the nation's count by where they lived as lines of the key (src/us/freeblack.js). Counts: U.S. Census Bureau, Working Paper No. 56 (data/us/census-free-slave-1790-1860.csv, scripts/census-wp56-free.mjs). Nothing is shaded by amount.

population.title: Native population
population._comment: From the first full census (1890) the states and territories are shaded by American Indians counted per 1,000 km² (src/us/native.js DENSITY_BREAKS, the same steps every year), with the largest counts as number badges. Before 1890 the census left most Native people out, so nothing is shaded: the scholarly estimates of data/us/native-estimates.csv speak instead, as badges with their ranges, and the national figure as a line of the legend.

military.title: Military
military._comment: The Military layer (brief of 2026-11-09; proposal P1, owner's defaults of the same day). Off by default: nothing changes unless tracker=military is asked for. Fills mean the side: each polygon takes its side's fill while its state is a member of the war shown (membership rows in the record table under tracker military; the war and its sides in vocab.json). Non-members are paper. Disputes keep their hatch, Native homelands their stipple. Which war: ?war=id, else the longest war alive on the date.

paths.title: How a place became a state
paths._comment: The statehood deck's Taxonomy 2 (brief of 2026-11-18, item 5): each state filled by the path it took into the Union, from a table, data/us/statehood-paths.csv (src/us/classify.js): one row per Newberry state id, with its source. Five fills: the owner lifted the four-fill limit for this tracker only (2026-11-18, "paths get 5"). A territory, not yet admitted, and the District stay paper. A highlight may name a path ("enabled") as well as states. The colors are the session's choice: five of Set A's six, the most widely spaced hues.

chapters.title: Statehood chapters
chapters._comment: Which chapter of the statehood deck each state is in, from data/us/statehood-chapters.csv (the outline's chapter map). The owner chose one chapter per slide (2026-11-18): an order lights a chapter ("chapter-3", or the states' ids) and its states take a fill; up to four chapters lit at once take one fill each, in chapter order, and a fifth is hatched (grammar §5). Without a highlight every state wears the neutral gray.

pieces.title: How the land became U.S. land
pieces._comment: The statehood deck's Taxonomy 1: the land each acquisition brought, credited to its last entry, computed by scripts/derive-pieces.mjs from the Newberry's own polygons and dated (data/us/pieces.topojson), labeled from data/us/acquisitions.csv. Four fills and Claimed hatched (owner, 2026-11-18: "Hatch Claimed"; West Florida, which Spain disputed). The states keep their borders and names over the pieces. A highlight of states draws only the pieces inside them. A piece with no label (Missouri Territory's claim south of the Red River, 1819) is paper. The colors are the session's choice.

electoral.title: Electoral College
electoral._comment: The latest presidential election held by the date shown, drawn on the map of its own day: each state filled by the candidate its electors voted for most (src/us/parties.json gives each party's fill), with its electoral votes as a number badge. Votes from the U.S. National Archives (data/us/electoral.json, scripts/fetch-electoral.mjs). Territories, and the District of Columbia before 1964, had no electors and stay muted.
